summary: [para 7] 7. During the hearing, the learned counsel for the Respondent, APDCL, referred to the APTEL judgment and also made detailed oral submissions on the issues viz., (i) time over-run of 671 days due to ethnic violence and bandhs, and (ii) time overrun of 30 days on account of the change in the course of the Champamati river. He also pointed out that the Petitioner, NTPC, failed to provide satisfactory reasons for enabling the Commission to condone the delay and accordingly, the claim of the Petitioner on this count, was rejected by the Commission vide its order dated 22.5.2017 (in Petition No. 45/GT/2016) and vide order dated 23.7.2018 in Petition No.29/RP/2017 filed by the Petitioner. While arguing that the Commission had elaborately dealt with the issue of ‘change in course of the Champamati river’ in an order dated 23.7.2018, the learned counsel submitted that there is little possibility that the water level can drastically go down in the said river, immediately after the high rainfall period. Accordingly, the learned counsel submitted that the reply filed in the matter may be considered while disposing of the petition. The representative of the Objectors adopted the above submissions of the Respondent, APDCL, and made oral submissions on the issues remanded by APTEL. The learned counsel for the Petitioner clarified that based on the orders passed in Petition No.45/GT/2016 (on remand), the consequential impact of the same shall be considered while passing the orders in the other tariff petitions, viz., 243/GT/2017 and 409/GT/2020, which had already been heard and orders reserved. Accordingly, based on the parties' consent, the order in the petitions, along with the IAs, was reserved. [para 8] 8. The Petitioner, in the IA and the note of arguments, has submitted the following: (a) As regards the issue (a)-time overrun for the period from April, 2013 to January, 2015 (671 days) on account of ethnic violence and bandh in the concerned area, the Commission had refused to condone the delay for the said period, except the period of 32 days, citing non-submission of prohibitory orders by NTPC during the time period in question. However, the APTEL has held that the Commission had taken note of only one page, which bears details of Section 144 prohibitory orders enforced between 2.5.2014 to 2.6.2014 and thus condoned the delay of these 32 days only. Whereas, the Petitioner had provided several other documents to support its claim that the project work was seriously impeded on account of violence and bandh from April 2013 to January 2015, but the same has not been considered. [¶] (e) The Commission in its order, had refused to condone the delay for the said period (671 days), except for the period of 32 days, on the ground of nonsubmission of the prohibitory orders issued during the time. However, APTEL has held that the Commission had taken note of only one page, which bears details of Section 144 CrPC enforced between 2.5.2014 and 2.6.2014 and thus condoned the delay of only 32 days. Whereas the Petitioner had provided several other documents to support its claim that the project work was seriously impeded on account of violence and bandh from April 2013 to January 2015, these were not considered.
